assessment.nobel_worthiness: Practical solid-state femtosecond lasers (Ti:sapphire gain medium, Kerr-lens mode-locking, semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors) are a clear invention that opened ultrafast science and underpins the attosecond methods recognised in 2023. Impact across spectroscopy, microscopy, metrology and industry is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Moulton demonstrated Ti:sapphire as a broadband laser medium; Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode-locking; Keller introduced SESAM-based passive mode-locking and scaled the technology. The three-way split maps to distinct, identifiable contributions, though priority around Kerr-lens mode-locking is shared with others I cannot confirm from memory.
assessment.maturity: Technology has been mature for three decades with abundant independent confirmation and widespread use; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Exact priority among mode-locking contributors beyond the credited names is uncertain.
Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the 2018 chirped-pulse amplification prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators and its first experimental realisation in HgTe wells opened a whole field of topological band materials, with lasting conceptual and material impact.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theory; Molenkamp led the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang theory prediction, who are not credited here, and Zhang is deceased). The credited trio is workable but leaves the HgTe theory prediction and 3D topological insulator experiments unrecognised.
assessment.maturity: Extensive independent confirmation in HgTe, Bi-based and other materials via transport and ARPES; the field is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Omission of the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and early 3D TI experimentalists complicates fairness.
Overlap with the separate quantum anomalous Hall candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles and experimental discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire materials field. This is a clear discovery with large, rapidly growing impact and strong materials-physics appeal, including heavy reliance on microscopy and spectroscopy for confirmation.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discoveries. Credit for related experimental work (e.g., other groups, STM studies) is not captured and might be contested.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups across platforms within a few years; interpretation of the superconductivity is still evolving, so some may judge it slightly early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unsettled.
Whether other experimental groups deserve co-recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock with magic-wavelength trapping gives unprecedented fractional uncertainty and stability and has reshaped precision measurement and time standards; the idea is original and the impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early clocks; Ye developed the leading strontium implementation reaching the 10^-18 level. A clean two-person allocation, although other lattice-clock groups and ion-clock work (Wineland-era) exist.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed by independent labs; accuracy well beyond the caesium standard is established. Redefinition of the second is pending, which may favour waiting slightly.
uncertainties: Relationship to previous prizes in precision timekeeping and ion clocks.
Whether the pending redefinition of the second would make a prize more timely.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for trapped-ion quantum gates and the experimental realisation of ion-trap quantum computation are foundational for controlled quantum information processing, with a path from concept to demonstrations of increasingly large devices.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the theoretical proposal; Blatt is a leading experimentalist with notable gate and algorithm demonstrations, but Wineland's NIST demonstrations and others (Monroe, Wineland already laureate in 2012) are also central. The credited triad is plausible but experimental credit is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Substantial independent confirmation across many ion-trap groups and companies; technology is advancing but scalable computation is not yet established.
uncertainties: Overlap with other candidates crediting Cirac and Zoller.
Experimental credit is shared with groups outside the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The qPlus sensor enabling atomic force microscopy with CO-functionalised tips yields sub-molecular and atomic resolution of structure and bond order. As an instrument invention with strong physical insight it fits the discovery-or-invention criterion, and it is close to my own methods field, so I rate it with an awareness of possible bias.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor; Gross and Meyer (IBM Zurich) demonstrated the CO-tip imaging of molecules. Reasonable allocation, though Binnig, Quate and Gerber (AFM) and Bian et al. context matter.
assessment.maturity: Method is widely adopted and independently reproduced across many labs; impact on surface science and chemistry is established though narrower than the top candidates.
uncertainties: Breadth of impact on physics specifically versus chemistry and surface science.
Potential professional bias from my own microscopy background.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of X-ray and optical afterglows localised gamma-ray bursts, establishing their cosmological distance and enabling redshifts and the supernova connection. This is a clean observational discovery of major impact.
assessment.attribution: BeppoSAX team (Costa, Frontera) first detected the X-ray afterglow; optical and radio identification and redshift work involved several groups, with Kulkarni, Djorgovski, van Paradijs and others. The three-name limit makes attribution contestable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed extensively over twenty-five years with many independent satellites and ground programs; recognition is mature, perhaps late.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among BeppoSAX and optical identification teams is difficult.
Astrophysics rather than my own area; my judgement is more general.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Photonic crystals introduced band gaps for light and control of spontaneous emission and propagation in periodic dielectrics, an original concept with broad use in nanophotonics, fibres and lasers.
assessment.attribution: Yablonovitch and John independently proposed photonic band gaps in 1987; Joannopoulos developed theory, modelling and 2D/3D structures. A defensible trio, though the experimental realisation and applications involved many others.
assessment.maturity: Concept is mature and verified in many systems; commercial and scientific uptake is large, with some applications being incremental.
uncertainties: Whether the impact is judged as more engineering than fundamental physics.
Credit for the first experimental 3D realisations.
